sanskrit: jīvātave na martave śiras ta ā rabhāmahe | rasaṃ viṣasya nāvidam udnaḥ phenam adann iva ||
english: For life, not for death, we take hold of your head. I have not found the essence of the poison — it is as though one had eaten the foam of water.

sanskrit: bhūmyā madhyād divo madhyād bhūmyā antād atho divaḥ | madhye pṛthivyā yad viṣaṃ tad vācā dūṣayāmasi ||
english: From the midst of the earth, from the midst of heaven, from the end of the earth, and likewise of the sky — whatever poison is in the middle of the earth, that we render inefficacious by our speech.

sanskrit: aśvatthe nihitaṃ viṣaṃ kapāle nihitaṃ viṣam | śilāyā jajñe taimātaḥ prathamo viṣadūṣaṇī ||
english: The poison deposited in the aśvattha tree, the poison deposited in the skull — born of the stone, the primordial taimāta, the first antidote to poison, has arisen.

sanskrit: viṣasyāhaṃ vaindakasya viṣasya dārvyasya ca | atho viṣasya svaitnasya samānīṃ vācam agrabham ||
english: Of the poison of the vaindaka plant, of the wooden poison, and likewise of the poison of the svaitna — I have grasped the same utterance that nullifies them all.

sanskrit: tad id vadanty arthina uta śūdrā utāryāḥ | viṣāṇāṃ viṣvagarthānāṃ sarvathaivārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: This indeed they declare — the supplicants, the Śūdras, and the Āryas alike: in every way the poison of all the various poisons is made devoid of potency.

sanskrit: paruṣas tvāmṛtakarṇo viṣa prathamam āvayat | yathā ha taṃ nāropayas tathāsy arasaṃ viṣam ||
english: O Poison, Paruṣa, the immortal-eared one, first turned you back. Just as you did not ascend into him, so also are you, O Poison, rendered without potency.

sanskrit: yad vo devā upajīkā uddehaṃ śuṣiraṃ daduḥ | tatrāmṛtasyāsiktaṃ tac cakārārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: What the gods gave to you, O upajīkā creatures — a hollow body, porous — therein ambrosia was poured in; that has rendered the poison without potency.

sanskrit: śakuntikā me abravīd viṣapuṣpaṃ dhayantikā | na ropayati na mādayaty arasaṃ śārvīyaṃ viṣam ||
english: The little bird śakuntikā told me, she who sucks the poison-flower: "The śārvīya poison does not cause infection, does not intoxicate — it is without potency."

sanskrit: aty apaptāma durgāṇi śārīḥ śakunayo yathā | ihendrāṇīṃ varuṇānīṃ sinīvālīṃ krakoḍhyām | grāhāṃ śūraputrāṃ devīṃ yācāmo viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: We have flown across the difficulties like the śārī birds and the śakunas. Here we beseech Indrāṇī, Varuṇānī, Sinīvālī, Krakoḍhyā, Grāhā — the divine daughter of the hero — for the antidote to poison.

sanskrit: ālakaṃ vyālakaṃ vy āvaṃ jālma jīgīmahe | jaradviṣaṃ yuvābhiṣag vayam it sāsahāmahai ||
english: The ālaka, the vyālaka — we have driven them away, O fool! We shall indeed overcome the aged poison, for youth itself is the physician.

sanskrit: asthād dyaur asthāt pṛthivy asthād viśvam idaṃ jagat | asthur viṣasyāropayo 'naḍvāhaḥ kriśā iva ||
english: Heaven has stood firm, the earth has stood firm, this entire world has stood firm. The toxic ascents of the poison have halted, like lean bullocks that can go no further.

sanskrit: yāvat sūryo vitapati yāvac cābhivipaśyati | tenāham indradattena kṛṇomy arasaṃ viṣam | tad viṣam arasaṃ viṣam adhobhāg arasaṃ viṣam ||
english: As far as the sun shines with warmth and as far as it gazes upon all things — by that Indra-granted power I make the poison devoid of potency. That poison is without potency, that poison is without potency — below is the poison without potency.

sanskrit: mātariśvā sam abharad dhātā sam adadhāt paruḥ | indrāgnī abhy arakṣatāṃ tvaṣṭā nābhim akalpayat ||
english: Mātariśvan assembled it; Dhātā knit the joints together. Indra and Agni guarded it about; Tvaṣṭā fashioned the navel.

sanskrit: bhavas tvā abhy arukṣad rudras te aṃsum ābharat | rātrī tvābhy agopāyat sā tvaṃ bhūte ajāyathāḥ ||
english: Bhava anointed you; Rudra brought you your shoot. Night guarded you on all sides — thus were you born, O plant-being.

sanskrit: dyauṣ ṭa āyur gopāyad antarikṣam asuṃ tava | mātā bhūtasya bhavyasya pṛthivī tvābhi rakṣatu ||
english: Heaven guarded your life-span; the atmosphere preserved your vital breath. May the earth, the mother of what has been and what shall be, protect you on all sides.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvā devāḥ samadadhuḥ sahasrapuruṣaṃ satīm | sā devī tvam asyedam apāja vy ajā viṣam ||
english: You whom the gods have assembled as the truly thousandfold being — you, that divine one, have expelled and scattered this poison here.

sanskrit: yāḥ purastāt prasyandante divā naktaṃ ca yoṣitaḥ | āpaḥ puru sravantīs tā u te viṣadūṣaṇīḥ ||
english: Those maiden streams that flow forth from the east by day and by night, the waters flowing copiously — they indeed are your antidotes to poison.

sanskrit: ātapas te varṣam āsīd agniś chāyābhavat tapaḥ | ulbaṃ te abhram āsīt sā tvaṃ bhūte ajāyathāḥ ||
english: The heat became your rain; fire became the shade that was your warmth. The cloud became your caul — thus were you born, O plant-being.

sanskrit: gandharvas te mūlam āsīc chākhā apsarasas tava | marīcīr āsan parṇāni sinīvālī kulaṃ tava ||
english: A Gandharva was your root; the Apsarases were your branches. Rays of light were your leaves; Sinīvālī was your lineage.

sanskrit: ajarā devā adadhur amṛtaṃ martyeṣv ā | tasyai tad agram ā dade tad u te viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: The ageless gods have placed ambrosia here among mortals. I take of that first portion of hers — and that is your antidote to poison.

sanskrit: anabhrau khanamānaṃ vipraṃ gambhīre apasam | bhiṣak cakṣur bhiṣak khane tad u te viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: In the two cloudless heavens, in the deep workings, the inspired one who digs — the physician is the eye, the physician is the digging-tool; and that is your antidote to poison.

sanskrit: yāḥ purastād vitiṣṭhante gāvaḥ pravrājinīr iva | amṛtasyeva vā asy atho hāsy arundhatī ||
english: Those that stand spread out in the east like wandering cattle — you are as if of ambrosia; and you shall indeed be Arundhatī.

sanskrit: yo mayaḥ saraghāyāḥ prakhāya madhv ābharat | tato yavaḥ prājāyata so 'bhavad viṣadūṣaṇaḥ ||
english: He who, for delight, having dug open the bee-nest, brought forth honey — from that barley was born; it became the antidote to poison.

sanskrit: yavasyaitat palālino godhūmasya tilasya ca | vrīher yavasya daivyena kṛṇomy arasaṃ viṣam ||
english: This — the straw of barley, of wheat, of sesame, of rice, of barley — by the divine power of barley I make the poison devoid of potency.

sanskrit: mahīṃ yoniṃ samudrasya- -anv avindann ṛtāyavaḥ | tāṃ devā guhyām āsīnāṃ samudrāc cid ud ābharan ||
english: The great womb of the ocean — those who are devoted to cosmic order found it. That one, sitting hidden, the gods carried upward even from the sea.

sanskrit: samudrāc cid udābhṛtya tām u puṣkara ā dadhuḥ | asyāḥ pṛthivyā devyāś cakṣur ākāśyam asi viṣadūṣaṇam ||
english: Having carried her upward even from the sea, they placed her in the lotus. You are the skyward eye of this divine earth, the antidote to poison.

sanskrit: samānam arthaṃ paryanti devā rūpaṃrūpaṃ tapasā vardhamānāḥ | yad ādityam abhisaṃviśanti tad ekaṃ rūpam amṛtatvam eṣām ||
english: The gods go about the same purpose, growing form by form through their austerity. When they enter into the Āditya, that is the one form — the immortality of them.

sanskrit: devo devebhir ā gaman mahān no atithiṣ pitā | sa praiti jātavedasam ekarūpo guhā bhavan ||
english: The god, great and our father-guest, has come among the gods. He goes forward to Jātavedas, becoming single-formed as he enters the hidden realm.

sanskrit: ātithyam agniṃ nir apaptad eva ubhayebhiḥ pitṛbhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ | mahān nu marya upa bhakṣam āgan saṃgṛbhyādityā(n) ny aviṣṭa vahniḥ ||
english: The fire of hospitality has indeed gone forth, consenting with the forefathers of both kinds. The great one has truly come near to partake, O mortal; the carrier-fire, having gathered the Ādityas, has entered in.

sanskrit: ta ā viśanti puruṣaṃ śayānaṃ prāṇā niviṣṭā na śasanty enam | te no rātryā sumanasyamānā ahnā rakṣanty ahṛṇīyamānāḥ ||
english: They enter into the sleeping person — the vital breaths, having settled in, do not injure him. They, disposed to goodwill toward us through the night, guard us through the day without animosity.

sanskrit: paśubhyo naḥ paśupate mṛḍa sarva saṃ vṛha āyatām | mā naḥ prāṇeṣu rīriṣaḥ ||
english: O Paśupati, lord of livestock, be gracious to us and to our animals; bring them all together and let them come home. Do not cause us injury in our vital breaths.

sanskrit: vāyuḥ satye adhiśritaḥ prāṇāpānāv abhirakṣan | saṃ prajā airayad imāḥ ||
english: Vāyu, established in truth, guarding the in-breath and the out-breath, has stirred these creatures into motion.

sanskrit: devā yattāḥ prajāpatāv ādityāś ca yemire | pūṣā raśmiṣv āyata ādityo viṣṇur ākrame sa rohaṃ divi rohati ||
english: The gods stood ready in Prajāpati; the Ādityas took their stations. Pūṣan extended himself into the rays of light; the Āditya-Viṣṇu strode forward with his strides — he who ascends climbs into the sky.

sanskrit: prajāddevāḥ savituḥ save tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu | añjantau madhunā payo atandraṃ yātam aśvinā ||
english: At the impulsion of Savitṛ may the gods beget offspring; may Tvaṣṭā fashion the forms. Come, O Aśvins, anointing the milk with sweetness, without fatigue.

sanskrit: viśve devāḥ pra yātana- -ādityāsaḥ sajoṣasaḥ | puraḥ paścāt svastaye ||
english: Go forth, O All-gods, O Ādityas in unison — in front and behind, for our well-being.

sanskrit: brahma varma bṛhaspatiḥ saṃgavo no 'bhi rakṣatu | devo devaiḥ purohitaḥ ||
english: May Bṛhaspati be the armor of sacred power; may he protect us at the gathering of cattle. The god, the purohita of the gods.

sanskrit: maruto vṛṣṭyā na ā gata satyadharmāṇa ūtaye | aparāhneṣu jinvata ||
english: Come to us, O Maruts, with rain — you of true dharma — for our aid. Quicken us in the afternoon hours.

sanskrit: indro rājā divas patir ahar vimāya tiṣṭhati | sa na imāḥ kalpayād diśaḥ ||
english: Indra, the king, the lord of heaven, stands measuring out the day. May he arrange these directions for us.
